A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DABand research work. All 23 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including Appendices A–H, are readable, and their methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original target-domain accuracy experiments in Tables 1–3, cumulative-regret experiments in Figure 1, and component ablations in Tables 4–5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark, cumulative-regret and ablation results in Tables 1–5 and Figure 1.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, LinUCB updates, adversarial alignment and training losses remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 newly specifies Adam without establishing an optimizer change. The corrected indicator placement in the theoretical bound already appeared in v2's implemented per-round reward penalty.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MNIST-to-MNIST-M, VisDA17 synthetic-to-real adaptation and the same ten-class S2RDA49 subset. Zero-shot evaluation and continued training with target feedback are retained; Figure 2 identifies no additional dataset or task.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figure 1 retain LinUCB, LinUCB-P, NLinUCB and NLinUCB-P, with the same LinUCB out-of-memory exclusions. Tables 4–5 retain the same ablation variants. The newly discussed distributionally robust bandit work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The documented splits, preprocessing, hyperparameters, 300/100-episode training budgets, 64-sample episodes and 1,920-round target evaluation are unchanged. Figure 2 adds component trajectories but does not document a separate or revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.1 and Figure 2 examine cumulative growth of individual regret-bound components and their sum against linear reference curves, addressing the sublinearity question. The existing regression-error, predicted-reward and discriminator ablations in Tables 4–5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain five runs with different random seeds for Figure 1, identical tabulated uncertainty values, and Appendix E's p-value range of 3.201e-21 to 1.504e-2. Figure 2 supplies no additional run-count, uncertainty or significance information.

E6.justification: Figure 2 adds plotted cumulative trajectories for source regret, regression error, predicted rewards, data divergence and the sum of other terms. All five tables and Figure 1 retain their results, including DABand average accuracies of 0.6002, 0.4644 and 0.3923 on the three benchmarks.

T1.justification: v3 moves the round-dependent action indicator inside the summation in Equation (5), Lemma A.6 and Theorem A.1, and repairs an incomplete predicted-reward expression in the discussion. Appendix G.1 adds an Adam-based sublinearity argument. The main bound structure remains, and the final line of Appendix A.2 still retains the old indicator placement.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same main claims: a first general domain-adaptive contextual-bandit method, learning from source-only feedback, a sublinear target-regret bound and superior benchmark performance. The added uncertainty-quantification suggestion concerns future work.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds an explanation of LinUCB and NLinUCB failures through their lack of explicit domain alignment and the divergence term. Appendix G.1 adds an optimization-based explanation for sublinearity. Appendix F's existing limitations concerning alignment quality, domain shift and interpretability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 now explicitly names Adam for encoder and discriminator updates. The abstract adds a repository link with a promise that code will become available; this does not establish released code. Appendix D's preprocessing, hardware and hyperparameter information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a paragraph distinguishing DABand from Si et al. (2023) on distributionally robust batch contextual bandits. Additional citations cover domain adaptation, Adam, uncertainty quantification, Bayesian deep learning and interpretability, while the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized explanatory additions, inserts Appendix G.1 and acknowledgments, and replaces duplicated novelty discussion with a cross-reference. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact. Author formatting and the conference-status header are updated.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 2, places Table 4 beside its ablation discussion instead of the conclusion, and compacts the author block. Existing tables and Figure 1 retain their display content, with limited surrounding layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves mathematical precision, implementation documentation and research positioning through the indicator-summation corrections, explicit Adam specification and added related-work comparison. The existing empirical evidence is preserved. The theoretical gain is limited: Appendix G.1 does not establish why Adam's optimizer-regret rate bounds every cumulative loss term, Figure 2 lacks dataset and run details, and the proof retains an inconsistent final expression. These additions do not establish a repaired general sublinearity guarantee.
